headline: Ferry manifest missed 46 people
deck: The MV Barima’s manifest listed 133 people. Investigators later established that 179 were aboard, exposing an accounting failure that complicated the search while a commission examines why the ferry capsized.
body: The MV Barima sailed from Georgetown for Port Kaituma on 18 July with an official manifest listing 116 passengers and 17 crew, a total of 133 people. [E1] Investigators later established that 179 people had been aboard. [E2] The difference between those official totals is 46 people. [E1][E2] The revised count emerged after survivors were found who had not appeared on the original list. [E2]

Officials first confirmed the rescue of 53 people. [E1] By 21 July, authorities reported 77 survivors and 41 bodies recovered after revising the onboard total to 179. [E2] On the evening of 23 July, the government said 72 bodies had been recovered, 65 of them identified, while the search continued. [E3] Those updates should not be converted into a final missing count while recovery, identification and survivor accounting remain active. [E3]

Guyana’s original manifest did not enumerate the human load that investigators later established. [E1][E2] That documented failure made rescue accounting harder because the departure list could not provide a complete denominator for the search. [E1][E2] Teams had to reconcile reported survivors and recoveries against a passenger total that changed after the capsize. [E1][E2][E3] The paper record therefore became part of the emergency, even before investigators determined what caused the vessel to overturn. [E4]

Guyana’s government has announced an independent Commission of Inquiry as a priority. [E4] The commission must determine the cause of the capsize and assign responsibility on the evidence. [E4] The 46-person discrepancy requires no conclusion about either question. [E1][E2] It is already established as the difference between the original manifest and the later official count aboard. [E1][E2]

MARAD’s director-general said the vessel was certified to carry up to 394 passengers and 126 tonnes, depending on its configuration, and said there was no evidence of overloading at that stage. [E5] That is the strongest null: the revised count of 179, by itself, does not establish overloading. [E2][E5] The inquiry has not established overloading or a mechanical cause. [E4][E5] The manifest failure stands separately as a documented accounting breakdown. [E1][E2]

International crews were working to salvage the capsized vessel while the death toll rose. [E6] The government’s search remained active through the evening of 23 July. [E3] The operation had to reconcile physical recoveries, survivor reports and identifications against the corrected onboard count. [E2][E3] Uncertainty in that process belongs to continuing accounting and should not be turned into a final missing figure. [E2][E3]

The state ferry corridor from Georgetown toward Port Kaituma depends on a paper boundary at embarkation. [E1] The manifest was that boundary, and it failed to enumerate 46 people later counted aboard. [E1][E2] The Commission of Inquiry may assign responsibility for the capsize after examining the evidence. [E4] Before it does, the departure record has already failed its most basic test: counting the people aboard. [E1][E2]
